title: Creatinine Test
attribution: Source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine.
measures: Creatinine is a waste product made when muscles are used and muscle tissue breaks down. The test checks blood or urine levels to assess kidney health and help diagnose or monitor kidney disease.
low: A low blood creatinine may signal malnutrition or a condition that makes muscles shrink, such as a long illness, a nerve disorder or muscle loss with age. Serious liver disease can also cause low levels.
high: A high blood creatinine may signal kidney disease or injury, such as infection, poor blood flow to the kidneys, a urinary blockage or kidney failure, and can also be linked to heart failure or diabetes. Causes outside the kidney include dehydration, muscle disorders and injuries, muscular dystrophy, intense exercise, a diet high in meat and certain pregnancy problems.
notes: Normal levels vary with muscle mass, diet, age and activity, and a normal result does not always mean healthy kidneys. Meat can temporarily raise creatinine.
